Package com.egradx.auth.config

Class EgradxAuthSchemaMigrator

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.config.EgradxAuthSchemaMigrator
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean
public class EgradxAuthSchemaMigrator extends Object implements org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean
Applies this library's migrations, from db/egradx-auth/<vendor>/, into its own history table so they don't compete with the application's own migrations for version numbers.

Order at startup: these first, then the application's own Flyway migrations (an application's tables reference egradx_organization), then the EntityManagerFactory, so that ddl-auto: validate sees the tables.

Deliberately not a Flyway bean. Spring Boot's own Flyway auto-configuration backs off when one exists, so exposing this library's Flyway as a bean would quietly stop the application's migrations from running.

Adopting an existing schema. Before this library migrated its own tables, each application created them from copies of these migrations. Such a database has the tables but no "egradx_auth_schema_history". Running V1 there would fail on the existing tables, so the version the tables are at is worked out from what each migration introduced (MARKERS), recorded as the baseline, and only the later migrations are applied.
